cards.text: Jesus just raised a widow's only son back to life in a town called Nain, and the news is spreading through Judea and all around it. Now it reaches John the Baptist, the prophet who preached a baptism of repentance around the Jordan. John's disciples tell him about all these things.

cards.question: John calls two of his disciples and sends them to Jesus with a question. What does John want to know?

answers.text: If Jesus is the One who was to come
If Jesus will come and baptize with him
If Jesus will teach them how to pray

cards.text: The two men find Jesus and repeat John's question word for word: "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" Not one word added, not one word dropped, which is more than any group chat has EVER done.

cards.question: True or false: At that very hour, before Jesus answers John's men, He heals many people and gives sight to many who are blind.
Jesus doesn't give John's men a plain yes or no. What does He tell them to report back to John?

answers.text: What they have seen and heard
That John should come and see
That they must wait for a sign

cards.text: Then Jesus spells it out: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear and the dead are raised. John asks a yes or no question, and Jesus sends back a HIGHLIGHT REEL.

cards.question: There's one more thing on Jesus' list, for people who don't usually hear good news first. The good news is preached to the ___.
Jesus adds one last line for John's men to carry back. True or false: Jesus says, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me."

cards.text: After John's messengers leave, Jesus asks the crowds what they went out into the wilderness to see: "A reed swaying in the wind?" Friend, NOBODY hikes out into the wilderness to watch a plant wiggle.

cards.question: Next Jesus asks if the crowds went out to see a man in fine clothes. True or false: Jesus says people who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in the wilderness.

cards.text: Third guess, and Jesus asks it straight: "What then did you go out to see? A prophet?" Then He answers His own question.

cards.question: Jesus asks the crowds if they went out to see a prophet. What is His answer about John?

answers.text: Yes and more than a prophet
No he is only a teacher
Not yet but someday he will be

cards.text: Jesus says John is the one Scripture already wrote about, in the words of the prophet Malachi (Malachi 3:1). In it, God says He will send His messenger ahead.

cards.question: In the Scripture Jesus quotes about John, God's messenger goes ahead to ___ the way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says that among those born of women, there is NO ONE greater than John. That's a greatest of all time title straight from Jesus, but He's not done.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says even the least in the kingdom of God is still not as great as John.

cards.text: All the people who hear this acknowledge God's justice, even the tax collectors. When the TAX COLLECTORS are nodding along, you know something big is going on.

cards.question: The people who hear Jesus, even the tax collectors, acknowledge God's justice. What reason does the passage give?

answers.text: They had paid back what they owed
They had given money to the poor

cards.question: The Pharisees, a strict group of Jewish religious leaders, and the experts in the law reject God's purpose for themselves. Why? They had not been ___ by John.

cards.text: Jesus is still talking to the crowds, and now He asks, "To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?" He's about to answer with a picture.

cards.question: What picture does Jesus use to describe the men of this generation?

cards.text: The children call out to one another: "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep." Happy tune or sad song, everybody just STANDS there like it's the office birthday party nobody signed up for.

cards.question: True or false: In Jesus' picture, the other children dance to the flute but won't weep at the dirge.

cards.text: Then Jesus explains the picture. John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine.

cards.question: John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine. What do people say about him?

cards.text: Then Jesus, the Son of Man, comes eating and drinking, and they call Him a glutton and a drunkard. I shared a junk drawer with dead batteries that argued all day, and even THEY were easier to please.

cards.question: Along with glutton and drunkard, people call Jesus a friend of tax collectors and ___.

cards.text: Jesus closes the whole comparison with one short line about wisdom and her children. Short, quiet, and it lands like a mic drop.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus ends by saying wisdom is forgotten by all her children.

findings.problem: The opening card states Bible facts from outside the passage with no reference: Jesus raising the widow's son at Nain and the news spreading through Judea (Luke 7:11-17), and John as the prophet who preached a baptism of repentance around the Jordan (Luke 3:3). The card cites only Luke 7:18.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The setup in the question ('for people who don't usually hear good news first') rules out 'priests' and 'kings', so only one answer is left. It is also Papa Dorin's own reading. Luke 7:22 doesn't say it.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The true or false card asks whether Jesus said an exact line (Luke 7:23) that no card has set up. The baker can't reason it out. The only way to answer is to guess whether the wording is real.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'block' and 'hide' don't make sense for a messenger God sends ahead. That makes them silly next to 'prepare', and the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card quotes 'you did not dance' and 'you did not weep' (Luke 7:32), which gives away the answer to the true or false question on card 4.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke compares people who can't be pleased (Luke 7:33-34) to dead batteries that 'argued all day.' Arguing isn't the same action as refusing to be pleased, so 'even THEY were easier to please' doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: No card ever says what Luke 7:35 says. Card 9 only mentions 'one short line about wisdom and her children,' and card 10's statement is false. The baker leaves without ever seeing that wisdom is vindicated by all her children.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 9 gives no context about what Jesus says about wisdom, so the baker can't reason out whether 'wisdom is forgotten by all her children' is true or false. It's a coin flip.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
